note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BRU 8; A06b BRU 8; L05 BRU 9(5)(a)): ordinary naturalisation after 20 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), A01b (descent, born abroad: Group restriction: only if citizen parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), A02a (birth in country: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from the father only, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a restriction to members of a particular group, which the form holds only in the condition's words, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file. On 2026-11-03 the primary was read: Laws of Brunei, Chapter 15, Brunei Nationality, Revised Edition 2011 (B.L.R.O. 9/2011), Attorney General's Chambers; listed 'In force' at https://www.agc.gov.bn/documents/brunei-nationality-act/. Every figure the file holds now rests on it, and the dataset is no longer cited. The Act asks no renunciation of another citizenship; its oath of allegiance (Second Schedule) has the applicant renounce loyalty to any other country, and an oath isn't a renunciation of citizenship, so renunciation stays false.

sources.said: 8. (1) His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan may ... grant to such person a certificate of naturalisation if he satisfies His Majesty ... that he — (a) has within the period of 25 years immediately preceding the date of his application resided in Brunei Darussalam for periods amounting in the aggregate to not less than 20 years; (b) has resided in Brunei Darussalam throughout the 2 years immediately preceding the date of his application; ... 9. (5) A person who has the status of a subject of His Majesty the Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan shall cease to have such status if — (a) he voluntarily acquires the nationality or citizenship of any State or country outside Brunei Darussalam ... 4. (1) ... the following persons, and no others, shall be subjects of His Majesty ... by operation of law — (a) any person born in Brunei Darussalam ... who is commonly accepted as belonging to one of the following indigenous groups of the Malay race, namely, Belait, Bisayah, Brunei, Dusun, Kedayan, Murut or Tutong ... (b) any person born in Brunei Darussalam ... whose father and mother were both born in Brunei Darussalam and are members of any of the groups of people specified in the First Schedule ... (c) any person born outside Brunei Darussalam ... (i) whose father was, at the time of birth of such person, a person born in Brunei Darussalam ... and was a person commonly accepted as belonging to one of the following indigenous groups ... Second Schedule, Oaths of Allegiance: I ... hereby declare on oath that I will not exercise the rights, powers and privileges to which I may be eligible by reason of any nationality or citizenship, and that I absolutely and entirely renounce and abjure all loyalty to any country, state or sovereign

atBirth.soilIf: Person is born in Brunei and belongs to one of the specified indigenous groups of the Malay race.; Person is born in Brunei to a father and mother who were both born in Brunei and are members of any of the groups of people specified in the 1st Schedule (i.e. people who are indigenous to Brunei, but note that the list is longer than the indigenous people referred to under BRU 4(1)a).
atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born abroad to a father who (1) was born in Brunei and belongs to one of the specified indigenous groups of the Malay race and (2) is employed abroad in the service of the Brunei government or a Brunei company. Or person is born to a father who was born abroad and who in turn was born to a father who was born in Brunei and belongs to one of the specified indigenous groups of the Malay race. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.; Person is born abroad to a father who (1) was born in Brunei to a mother and father who were both born in Brunei and are members of any of the groups of people specified in the 1st Schedule (i.e. people who are indigenous to Brunei, but note that the list is longer than the indigenous people referred to under BRU 4(1)a) and (2) is employed abroad in the service of the Brunei government or a Brunei company. Or person is born abroad to a father and mother who were both born in Brunei and are members of any of the groups specified in the 1st Schedule. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.; Person is born abroad to a father who is a citizen and is employed abroad in the service of the Brunei government or a Brunei company. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.; Person is born abroad to a father who is a citizen by registration or naturalisation. Child needs to be registered within 6 months after birth.
